phase1.intro:
Last lesson explained what FXML is; this one wires it to real, running behavior.

Where should we start?

topics.buttonText: How does an fx:id actually connect to a Java field?
dialogue: `fx:controller="MyController"` on the root tag tells FXMLLoader which class to instantiate. `fx:id="nameField"` names an element. In the controller, [[term:@FXML]] before a field — `@FXML private TextField nameField;` — tells FXMLLoader [[key:"inject the node with this fx:id into this field once loaded"]]. Field names must match fx:id exactly.

stickyNote.flavor: 🔌 fx:id in FXML, matching field name with @FXML
stickyNote.definition: fx:controller sets the controller class; fx:id names an element in FXML. @FXML on a matching field name injects that node once loaded.

topics.buttonText: What does the @FXML initialize() method do?
dialogue: A method annotated `@FXML void initialize()` runs automatically right after every @FXML field has been injected — the natural place to set up initial state, since you're guaranteed every field is already wired by the time it runs.

stickyNote.flavor: 🏁 runs after every field is already wired
stickyNote.definition: @FXML void initialize() runs automatically once all @FXML fields are injected — the right place to set initial state.

topics.buttonText: Are there any rules about the controller's constructor?
dialogue: [[warn:The controller class needs a public no-argument constructor]] (or none declared, which Java provides for free) — FXMLLoader constructs it via reflection behind the scenes, and reflection can't call a constructor that demands arguments it has no way to supply.

stickyNote.definition: A controller class needs a public no-argument constructor (or none declared) since FXMLLoader instantiates it via reflection.

phase1.output: (Window with working form — enter name and message, submit button enables, label updates)
phase1.openingDialogue: @FXML fields inject matching fx:id nodes, initialize() runs once they're all wired, and the controller needs a no-arg constructor. 🔌

phase2.errorMessage:
Exception in thread "JavaFX Application Thread" java.lang.NullPointerException
    at WrongController.handleEvent(WrongController.java:8)
    ...
(label is null because it wasn't injected!)
phase2.explanation:
[[warn:NullPointerException]] the instant the controller tries to use one of its @FXML fields.

This almost always comes down to one thing: [[key:the fx:id in the FXML file doesn't exactly match the field name in the controller]] — a typo, a case mismatch, or an fx:id that was renamed in one file but not the other. FXMLLoader matches purely by string comparison of names; it has no way to catch a mismatch at compile time, since the FXML file is just a resource, not code the compiler reads. The field gets left null, the layout renders perfectly fine, and the exception only shows up the moment your controller code tries to call a method on that null field — often on the very first click.

phase3.openingDialogue: FXML controllers — wire up your UI! 🔌

mcq.question:
An FXML file has <TextField fx:id="emailField" />. The controller declares @FXML private TextField emailFeild; (note the typo). What happens when the app runs?

A) A compile error, since fx:id and the field name must match
B) FXMLLoader auto-corrects small typos using fuzzy matching
C) emailFeild stays null — no compile-time link exists between an fx:id string and a field name
D) The FXML file fails to load at all

phase4.selfChallenge:
Create a controller for this FXML:

<VBox fx:controller="CalculatorController">
    <TextField fx:id="num1Field" promptText="Number 1" />
    <TextField fx:id="num2Field" promptText="Number 2" />
    <Label fx:id="resultLabel" text="Result: " />
    <HBox>
        <Button fx:id="addBtn" text="Add" onAction="#handleAdd" />
        <Button fx:id="subtractBtn" text="Subtract" onAction="#handleSubtract" />
    </HBox>
</VBox>

Write the CalculatorController class with:
1. @FXML fields for all elements
2. handleAdd() method that adds the two numbers
3. handleSubtract() method that subtracts the two numbers
4. initialize() method that sets up any initial state

Note: No need to write the full app — just the controller class.

phase5.trivia: [[fun:FXMLLoader needs your controller class to have a public no-arg constructor]] (or none declared, which Java supplies automatically) — it's constructing your controller via reflection, and reflection has no way to guess what arguments a custom constructor would want.
